originalTitle: Market cuts odds of Fed hike after jobs data, but economists still see case for tightening
simplifiedContent: Recently, the US reported weaker-than-expected job growth in July, which has lowered expectations that the Federal Reserve (the "Fed") will raise interest rates next month. As a result, investors now think it's less likely that the Fed will increase interest rates soon. Some Fed officials want to raise rates to help control inflation, but others are not so sure. The Fed is keeping a close eye on inflation to decide what to do with interest rates. This matters because changes in interest rates can affect the overall economy and the stock market.

originalTitle: Dollar falls against yen, euro as weak US jobs data clouds Fed outlook
simplifiedContent: The value of the US dollar went down compared to other important currencies, like the yen and euro, on Friday. This happened because the US job market didn't do as well as expected in July, with more people losing jobs than anticipated. Even though the percentage of people without jobs actually decreased, fewer people were working or looking for work, which is a concern. This news makes it less clear what the Federal Reserve (the "Fed") will do with interest rates, which is important for the economy. The drop in the dollar's value is a result of these mixed signals about the US economy.

originalTitle: Raymond Realty Q1 net profit falls 19 pc to Rs 13.43 cr on higher expenses
simplifiedContent: Raymond Realty, a real estate company, made 19% less profit in the first quarter of the year compared to last year. This happened because the company spent more on operations, which reduced its overall earnings. However, the company's total income actually increased to Rs 535.71 crore. The company also had a good quarter in terms of sales, with bookings of Rs 700 crore, which is more than double what it was last year. This news matters because it shows how the company is performing financially, which can help investors decide whether to buy or sell its stock.

originalTitle: Sebi to cut routine checks by two-thirds, focus on high-risk players
simplifiedContent: The stock market regulator, Sebi, is changing how it checks on companies and investors. It will reduce the number of routine checks it does by about two-thirds, which means it will only do about one-third as many inspections as it did last year. This new approach is meant to make Sebi's work more efficient. By doing fewer routine checks, Sebi can focus on looking closely at companies and investors that are considered high-risk, which can help keep the market safe. This change matters because it could help Sebi catch and prevent more serious problems in the market.

originalTitle: Weekly Winner: Ujaas Energy jumps 68% this week as upbeat Q1 earnings fuel buying
simplifiedContent: Ujaas Energy's stock price increased by 68% this week, ending at ₹257.80. This happened because the company released its quarterly earnings report, which showed that it made more money than expected. Specifically, its net profit (or total earnings) went up by 31% compared to the same time last year. The main reason for this increase was that the company sold more solar power systems, which brought in more revenue. This is important because it shows that the company is doing well, which is why investors are eager to buy its stock.

originalTitle: Cupid net profit jumps 194% YoY to  ₹44 crore in Q1 as margins expand sharply; raises FY27 guidance
simplifiedContent: Cupid, a company, made a lot more money in the first quarter of this year compared to the same time last year. Its net profit, which is the amount of money it has left after paying all its expenses, increased by 194% to ₹44 crore. The company's revenue, which is the total amount of money it made from selling its products or services, also increased by 142% to ₹157 crore. This growth was largely due to its international and domestic healthcare businesses doing very well. This is significant because it shows that Cupid's business is performing well, which could be good news for people who have invested in the company.
